2027-05-12.title: Seventh Wednesday of Resurrection

readings: God is love; he has given us of his Spirit
This is eternal life: that they may know you
2027-05-12.alt: Season of the Resurrection (Qyamta), in the days between the Ascension and Pentecost. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and the Queen of Heaven (Regina Caeli) is prayed in place of the Angelus until Pentecost. The sixth day of the novena to the Holy Spirit. In the Latin calendar, Sts Nereus and Achilleus, martyrs, and St Pancras, martyr (optional memorials).
2027-05-12.verse: And this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.
theo: On the night before he died, at the end of the Last Supper, Jesus lifted his eyes to heaven and prayed aloud before his disciples. The Church calls this prayer, which fills the seventeenth chapter of John, the prayer of the Hour or the high-priestly prayer. “Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son so that the Son may glorify you.” The hour is the hour of the Cross, and Jesus calls it glory. On the Cross the love of the Father and the Son is shown to the world, and through the Cross the Son returns to the glory he had “before the world existed”. We read this prayer in the days after the Ascension because the prayer has been answered: the Son has been glorified and has gone back to the Father. But the prayer has not ended. The Letter to the Hebrews says that the Risen Lord “always lives to make intercession” for us (Hebrews 7:25). What Jesus prayed in the upper room he goes on praying at the Father's right hand, and in these nine days the Church in the upper room joins her prayer to his.

At the centre of the prayer is a definition: “And this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.” Eternal life is not first of all a long life after death; it is a relationship that begins now. In the Bible to know someone is more than to know facts about him; it is to love him, to share his life, as husband and wife know each other. So eternal life is to know the Father and the Son in the love of the Holy Spirit. A child preparing for First Holy Communion who learns to talk to Jesus has begun eternal life. An old grandmother saying her rosary in the evening is living it. Jesus adds, “I glorified you on earth by finishing the work that you gave me to do.” His whole life was obedience, and that obedience is his glory. We too glorify God not by great deeds but by doing faithfully the work he gives us, in the kitchen, the classroom, the hospital ward, the field.

The First Letter of John shows what that knowledge looks like in practice. “No one has ever seen God; if we love one another, God lives in us, and his love is perfected in us.” We cannot see God, but we can see our brother, and in loving him the invisible God becomes present. Then comes the link with Pentecost: “By this we know that we abide in him and he in us, because he has given us of his Spirit.” The Spirit is the gift that makes this love possible. John puts it in words that sum up the whole Gospel: “God is love, and those who abide in love abide in God, and God abides in them.” And he draws a bold consequence: “There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear.” Many Christians live with a fearful religion, afraid of God as of a harsh judge. John says that the closer we come to God's love, the less room fear has. But he will not let us escape into sweet feelings: “Those who say, ‘I love God,’ and hate their brothers or sisters, are liars.” On this day of the novena we ask the Spirit for a love that is real: love that casts out fear before God and love that reaches the brother we can see.
conn: “I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you” (Jeremiah 31:3).
“For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings” (Hosea 6:6).
“Consequently he is able for all time to save those who approach God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them” (Hebrews 7:25).
“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God” (John 1:1); “we have seen his glory, the glory as of a father's only son” (John 1:14).
“God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit that has been given to us” (Romans 5:5).
“Do not fear, for I am with you, do not be afraid, for I am your God” (Isaiah 41:10).
altar: The prayer of John 17 was spoken at the table of the Last Supper. In every Holy Qurbana the Lord who prayed that night offers himself to the Father, and the Church prays with him and through him, in the Holy Spirit.
In Communion we come to know him in the deepest way: not only by hearing about him but by receiving him. Let that knowledge become love for the brothers and sisters who receive him beside us.
outline: The night before he died, Jesus lifts his eyes to heaven and prays.
Point 1 · Father, the hour has come
The Cross as glory, and the High Priest who still intercedes.
To know the Father and the Son: a relationship that begins now.
Point 3 · God is love; perfect love casts out fear
The Spirit's gift, the brother we can see, and a faith without fear.
A grandmother in Changanacherry saying her rosary at dusk, at home with God.
“God is love, and those who abide in love abide in God.”
live: Read John 17 slowly this week, a few verses each day, and join your prayer to the prayer of Jesus.
Know him, not only about him (John 17:3)
Spend ten minutes today speaking to Jesus as to a friend, before the Blessed Sacrament if you can.
Love the brother you can see (1 John 4:20)
Do one concrete act of love today for someone you find difficult.
Let love cast out fear (1 John 4:18)
Name one fear you carry before God, and entrust it to his love in the novena prayer.
fathers: Love, and do what you will. If you keep silence, keep silence out of love; if you cry out, cry out out of love; if you correct, correct out of love; if you spare, spare out of love. Let the root of love be within you; from this root nothing but good can grow.

The glory of God is a human being fully alive, and the life of a human being is the vision of God. If the revelation of God through creation gives life to all who live on earth, how much more does the manifestation of the Father through the Word give life to those who see God.
magis: St John goes even further when he affirms that “God is love”: God's very being is love. By sending his only Son and the Spirit of Love, God has revealed his innermost secret: God himself is an eternal exchange of love, Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

When his hour had come, Jesus prayed to the Father. His prayer, the longest transmitted by the Gospel, embraces the whole economy of creation and salvation; it is the prayer of our High Priest, inseparable from his sacrifice.
Charity is the theological virtue by which we love God above all things for his own sake, and our neighbour as ourselves for the love of God. It is the form of all the virtues.
saints: 7–13 May: the days after the Ascension of our Lord (Thursday 6 May), when the apostles waited in prayer for the Holy Spirit “together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus” (Acts 1:14). Many families and parishes pray a novena to the Holy Spirit from Friday 7 to Saturday 15 May, the eve of Pentecost. Fri 7: First Friday. Sun 9: Seventh Sunday of Resurrection, the Sunday after the Ascension; the Latin Church in India celebrates the Ascension on this Sunday. Mon 10: in the Latin calendar, St John of Avila. Wed 12: in the Latin calendar, Sts Nereus and Achilleus and St Pancras. Thu 13: in the Latin calendar, Our Lady of Fatima. The Marian month of May continues (verify locally).
2027-05-12.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, on the night of your Passion you lifted your eyes to heaven and prayed for us, and now at the Father's right hand you live for ever to intercede for us. Grant us eternal life: to know the Father, the only true God, and you whom he has sent. Pour into our hearts the Spirit of love, so that perfect love may cast out all fear, and we may love the brothers and sisters we can see. Let us glorify the Father by finishing the work he gives us each day. With Mary, who abode in your love, we pray: come, Holy Spirit. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Jesus prays: Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son. The Ascended Lord still intercedes for us.
This is eternal life: to know the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he has sent.
John: God is love; he has given us of his Spirit; perfect love casts out fear; love the brother you can see.
2027-05-12.action: Read John 17 slowly this week, and do one concrete act of love today for someone you find difficult.
2027-05-12.question: Is my faith ruled more by fear of God or by trust in his love?
kidsaint: Pancras was a boy who lived in Rome about three hundred years after Jesus. The old stories say that he became a Christian as a young teenager. When the emperor ordered Christians to give up their faith, Pancras, though he was only about fourteen, said that he would not deny Jesus, and he was put to death. A great church in Rome is named after him. Lesson: perfect love casts out fear; when we love Jesus, he makes us brave.
2027-05-12.special: Seventh Wednesday of Resurrection. Sixth day of the novena to the Holy Spirit. In the Latin calendar, Sts Nereus and Achilleus and St Pancras.
term: The name given since the sixteenth century to the prayer of Jesus in John 17, spoken at the Last Supper on the night before his Passion. In it Jesus prays for his own glorification, for his disciples and for all who will believe through their word, “that they may all be one”. It is the prayer of the High Priest who offers himself, and he continues it in heaven, where he “always lives to make intercession” for us (Hebrews 7:25).

family.explain: John tells us something wonderful: God is love! He loves us so much that he gives us his Holy Spirit, and when we love one another, God lives in us. John also says, ‘There is no fear in love.’ We do not need to be afraid of God; he is our Father who loves us. ‘We love because he first loved us.’
family.intention: We pray for people who are afraid, that they may feel God's love.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is one person in our family or class we can show God's love to tomorrow?”

illus: A young doctor from Changanacherry remembers how, as a boy, he was afraid of God. He thought of him as a stern headmaster with a book of marks. What changed him was not a sermon but his grandmother. Every evening at dusk she sat on the verandah with her rosary, talking to God and to Mary as if they were sitting beside her, sometimes laughing, sometimes crying, always at peace. One night he asked her, ‘Ammachi, are you not afraid of God?’ She looked at him in surprise. ‘Afraid? Monae, I have known him for eighty years.’ That, he says, was the first time he understood that eternal life is to know God, and that the more you know him, the less you fear.

pm.open: Father, your Son prayed for us on the night before he died, and he intercedes for us still. Pour your love into our hearts by the Holy Spirit as we gather. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Father, the hour has come (John 17:1). What “hour” of difficulty am I living, and can I see God's glory in it?
This is eternal life, that they may know you (John 17:3). Do I know God, or only know about him?
There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear (1 John 4:18). What fear keeps me from trusting God?
Those who do not love a brother or sister whom they have seen, cannot love God whom they have not seen (1 John 4:20). Whom do I find hardest to love?
pm.resp: Lord, abide in us, and let us abide in your love.
interc: For the Church, that her members may know the Father and the Son and live in love.
For Christians who live in fear of God, that they may discover his love.
For those who are persecuted for the faith, like the young martyrs of Rome, that perfect love may cast out their fear.
For families and communities divided by hatred, that the Spirit may make them one.
For our parish, that our love for God may be seen in our love for one another.
pm.close: Father, you are love, and you have given us your Spirit. Let us know you and your Son, abide in your love and love one another, through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

homily: Dear friends, on the night before he died, Jesus lifted his eyes to heaven and prayed: “Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son so that the Son may glorify you.” The hour was the Cross, and Jesus called it glory, because on the Cross God's love was shown to the world.

We read this prayer after the Ascension because it has been answered: Jesus has returned to the glory of the Father. But he has not stopped praying. He “always lives to make intercession” for us. In this novena, we join our prayer to his.

Jesus says: “This is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.” Eternal life begins now. To know God is not only to know facts about him; it is to love him and live with him, as a friend. A child who talks to Jesus has begun eternal life.

John tells us: “God is love, and those who abide in love abide in God.” God has given us his Spirit so that we can love. And “perfect love casts out fear.” We do not need to live afraid of God. But John adds: if you say you love God and hate your brother, you are a liar. Love for God must reach the brother we can see.
Let us ask the Holy Spirit today for this love: love that takes away fear, and love that reaches the people around us. Come, Holy Spirit! Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, John says: God is love! God loves you more than anyone can.
When we love one another, God lives in us. And when we know how much God loves us, we are not afraid. Today, say: ‘Jesus, I love you, and I am not afraid!’

sub: The Spirit, the gift that makes love possible.
q: Do not fear, for I am with you, do not be afraid, for I am your God; I will strengthen you, I will help you, I will uphold you with my victorious right hand.
There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear; for fear has to do with punishment, and whoever fears has not reached perfection in love.

concl: The Lord who prayed for us on the night before he died prays for us still, and gives us his Spirit of love.
To know him is eternal life; to love the brother is the proof that we know him.
2027-05-12.resolve: This week, pray John 17, speak to Jesus as a friend each day, and let love overcome one fear and one dislike.
